chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbihi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the sexually impure man (junub) who forgets and immerses his hand into a vessel before washing it: that there is no problem, provided that nothing (of the impurity) had reached his hand.

key_terms.أصاب يده شيء: Nothing reached/touched his hand — meaning no actual physical filth (najasa) contaminated the hand
key_terms.الإناء: Ina' — a vessel, container, or water receptacle used for purification
key_terms.الجنب: Junub — a person in a state of major ritual impurity (janaba) requiring ghusl, typically after sexual intercourse or ejaculation
key_terms.السهو: Sahu — forgetfulness, inadvertence, an unintentional act
key_terms.الغمس: Ghams — to immerse or dip (a hand or object into water)
key_terms.لا بأس: La ba's — 'there is no problem/harm', a common Shia juridical formula indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: If a junub man puts his hand in water before washing, is the water still pure?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addressed a question of ritual purity (tahara): if a man in a state of major ritual impurity (janaba) inadvertently dips his hand into a water vessel before performing the obligatory ritual washing (ghusl), this does not invalidate the water — as long as no physical impurity was actually present on his hand. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that ritual impurity (hadath) is a legal status, not necessarily a physical contamination, and that inadvertent acts (sahu) may be treated with leniency when no actual najasa (ritual filth) was transferred.
